sentences.zh: ◎賈杜令狐

translations.literal: ◎ Jia, Du, Linghu
translations.idiomatic: Biographies: Jia, Du, and Linghu

sentences.zh: =賈耽=

translations.literal: = Jia Dan =
translations.idiomatic: = Jia Dan =

sentences.zh: 賈耽，字敦詩，滄州南皮人。

translations.literal: Jia Dan, courtesy name Dunshi, was a man of Nanpi in Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Dan, whose courtesy name was Dunshi, came from Nanpi in Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，舉明經，補臨清尉。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era he passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed Linqing Assistant Magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao reign he passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed assistant magistrate of Linqing.

sentences.zh: 上書論事，徙太平。

translations.literal: He memorialized the throne on affairs of state and was transferred to Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: After he submitted a memorial discussing state affairs, he was transferred to Taiping.

sentences.zh: 河東節度使王思禮署為度支判官。

translations.literal: Hedong military governor Wang Silü appointed him fiscal commissioner adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Silü, military governor of Hedong, appointed him adjutant for fiscal affairs.

sentences.zh: 累進汾州刺史，治凡七年，政有異績。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to Prefect of Fenzhou; in all seven years of rule his administration had outstanding achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to prefect of Fenzhou, and in seven years of governance achieved remarkable results.

sentences.zh: 召授鴻臚卿，兼左右威遠營使。

translations.literal: Summoned and appointed Director of the Court for Diplomatic Relations, concurrently commander of the Left and Right Weiyuan camps.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court and made Director of the Court for Diplomatic Relations, while also commanding the Left and Right Weiyuan camps.

sentences.zh: 俄為山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: Soon he became military governor of Shannan West circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed military governor of the Shannan West circuit.

sentences.zh: 梁崇義反東道，耽進屯谷城，取均州。

translations.literal: Liang Chongyi rebelled in the East circuit; Dan advanced to encamp at Gucheng and seized Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Chongyi rebelled in the eastern circuit, Dan advanced to encamp at Gucheng and captured Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 建中三年，徙東道。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianzhong he was transferred to the East circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Jianzhong era he was transferred to the eastern circuit.

sentences.zh: 德宗在梁，耽使司馬樊澤奏事。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong was at Liang; Dan sent his chief of staff Fan Ze to report on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Dezong was at Liang, Dan dispatched his chief of staff Fan Ze to report to the throne.

sentences.zh: 澤還，耽大置酒會諸將。

translations.literal: When Ze returned, Dan held a grand banquet for the generals.
translations.idiomatic: When Ze returned, Dan gave a grand banquet for his generals.

sentences.zh: 俄有急詔至，以澤代耽，召為工部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon an urgent edict arrived appointing Ze to replace Dan and summoning Dan as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: An urgent edict soon arrived appointing Ze to replace Dan and summoning Dan to serve as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 耽納詔於懷，飲如故。

translations.literal: Dan tucked the edict into his robe and drank on as before.
translations.idiomatic: Dan slipped the edict into his robe and continued drinking as though nothing had happened.

sentences.zh: 既罷，召澤曰：「詔以公見代，吾且治行。」

translations.literal: When the feast ended he called Ze and said: "The edict appoints you to replace me; I shall soon make ready to depart.
translations.idiomatic: When the banquet ended he summoned Ze and said, "The edict appoints you to take my place; I shall soon prepare to leave.

sentences.zh: 敕將吏謁澤。

translations.literal: He ordered the officers and clerks to pay their respects to Ze.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered his officers and clerks to pay their respects to Ze.

sentences.zh: 大將張獻甫曰：「天子播越，而行軍以公命問行在，乃規旄鉞，利公土地，可謂事人不忠矣。

translations.literal: Grand general Zhang Xianfu said: "The Son of Heaven is in exile, yet the army sent you on his orders to inquire after the court's whereabouts—and you scheme for commander's insignia, seeking to profit from his territory. This is disloyalty to your lord.
translations.idiomatic: Grand general Zhang Xianfu said, "The Son of Heaven is wandering in exile, and the army sent you on his orders to learn where the court has gone—yet you plot for a commander's baton and staff, scheming to seize his territory. That is disloyalty to your lord.

sentences.zh: 軍中不平，請為公殺之。」

translations.literal: The army is discontent; I ask leave to kill him for you.
translations.idiomatic: The troops are angry; allow me to kill him for you.

sentences.zh: 耽曰：「是何謂邪？

translations.literal: Dan said: "What talk is this?
translations.idiomatic: Dan said, "What sort of talk is that?

sentences.zh: 朝廷有命，即為帥矣。

translations.literal: When the court has issued its command, he is commander.
translations.idiomatic: When the court issues its command, he is our commander.

sentences.zh: 吾今趨覲，得以君俱。」

translations.literal: I am hurrying to audience now and may have you all accompany me."
translations.idiomatic: I am hurrying to court now, and you may all come with me."

sentences.zh: 乃行，軍中遂安。

translations.literal: Then he departed, and the army was at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Then he set out, and the army was calmed.

sentences.zh: 俄為東都留守。

translations.literal: Soon he became custodian of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made custodian of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 故事，居守不出城，以耽善射，優詔許獵近郊。

translations.literal: By precedent the custodian did not leave the city; because Dan excelled at archery, an exceptional edict permitted him to hunt in the nearby suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: By custom a custodian did not leave the city, but because Dan was skilled at archery, a special edict allowed him to hunt in the nearby suburbs.

sentences.zh: 遷義成節度使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be military governor of Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as military governor of Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 淄青李納雖削偽號，而陰蓄奸謀，冀有以逞。

translations.literal: Li Na of Ziqing had shed his false title, yet secretly harbored treacherous designs, hoping for a chance to act.
translations.idiomatic: Li Na of Ziqing had abandoned his false title, yet secretly nursed treacherous schemes, hoping for a chance to carry them out.

sentences.zh: 其兵數千自行營還，道出滑，或謂館於外。

translations.literal: Several thousand of his troops returning from their own camp passed through Hua; some said they should be quartered outside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand of his troops were returning from their own camp and passed through Hua; some suggested quartering them outside the city.

sentences.zh: 耽曰：「與我鄰道，奈何疑之，使暴於野？」

translations.literal: Dan said: "They are from a neighboring circuit—why doubt them and leave them exposed in the open?
translations.idiomatic: Dan said, "They are from a neighboring circuit—why treat them with suspicion and leave them exposed in the open?

sentences.zh: 命館城中，宴廡下，納士皆心服。

translations.literal: He ordered them lodged in the city and entertained below the hall; Li Na's soldiers were all won over in heart.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered them lodged inside the city and entertained them below the hall, and Li Na's men were won over in heart.

sentences.zh: 耽每畋，從數百騎，往往入納境。

translations.literal: Whenever Dan went hunting he took several hundred horsemen and often rode into Li Na's territory.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Dan went hunting he took several hundred horsemen and often rode into Li Na's territory.

sentences.zh: 納大喜，然畏其德，不敢謀。

translations.literal: Li Na was greatly pleased, yet feared his virtue and dared not plot.
translations.idiomatic: Li Na was greatly pleased, yet feared Dan's moral authority and dared not plot against him.

sentences.zh: 貞元九年，以尚書右僕射同中書門下平章事，俄封魏國公。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhenyuan he was made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs with concurrent status as co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and soon enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Zhenyuan he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs with concurrent status as Grand Councilor, and soon enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 常以方鎮帥缺，當自天子命之，若謀之軍中，則下有背向，人固不安。

translations.literal: He often held that when a frontier command lacked a chief, appointment ought to come from the Son of Heaven himself; if it were plotted out in the army, subordinates would face both ways and people could not be secure.
translations.idiomatic: He often argued that when a frontier command lacked a leader, the appointment ought to come from the Son of Heaven; if the choice were plotted out in the army, subordinates would turn in different directions and no one could feel secure.

sentences.zh: 帝然之，不用也。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed and did not adopt military nomination.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed with him and did not adopt the practice.

sentences.zh: 順宗立，進檢校司空、左僕射。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shunzong acceded, Dan was advanced to honorary Grand Preceptor and Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shunzong came to the throne, Dan was promoted to honorary Grand Preceptor and Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 時王叔文等幹政，耽病之，屢移疾乞骸骨，不許。

translations.literal: Wang Shuwen and others were meddling in government; Dan was disgusted and repeatedly memorialized illness asking to retire, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shuwen and his faction were meddling in government; Dan was disgusted and repeatedly asked to retire on grounds of illness, but his requests were denied.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十六，贈太傅，謚曰元靖。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-six; posthumously made Grand Tutor with posthumous title Yuanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-six and was posthumously made Grand Tutor with the posthumous title Yuanjing.

sentences.zh: 耽嗜觀書，老益勤，尤悉地理。

translations.literal: Dan loved to read; he grew more diligent in old age and was especially versed in geography.
translations.idiomatic: Dan loved to read, and he grew only more diligent in old age; he was especially expert in geography.

sentences.zh: 四方之人與使夷狄者見之，必從詢索風俗，故天下地土區產、山川夷岨，必究知之。

translations.literal: Anyone from the four quarters or envoys to the barbarian tribes who met him was invariably questioned about local customs; thus products of all lands, mountains and rivers, heights and marshes—he sought to know them all thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who came from the four quarters or served as envoy to the barbarian tribes, upon meeting him, was invariably questioned about local customs; thus the products of every region, its mountains and rivers, its heights and marshes—he sought to master them all.

sentences.zh: 方吐蕃盛強，盜有隴西，異時州縣遠近，有司不復傳。

translations.literal: While Tibet was powerful and had seized Longxi, the former distances among prefectures and counties were no longer relayed by the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: While Tibet was strong and had seized Longxi, the old distances between prefectures and counties were no longer reported by the authorities.

sentences.zh: 耽乃繪布隴右、山南九州，且載河所經受為圖，又以洮湟甘涼屯鎮頟籍、道里廣狹、山險水原為《別錄》六篇、《河西戎之錄》四篇，上之。

translations.literal: Dan then painted and distributed [maps of] the nine prefectures of Longyou and Shannan, and also made a chart of the courses taken by rivers; further, using records of garrisons and registrations in Tao, Huang, Gan, and Liang, with distances broad and narrow, mountain hazards and water sources, he compiled six fascicles of Separate Records and four of Records of the Western He Xi Rong, and submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: Dan then painted and distributed maps of the nine prefectures of Longyou and Shannan, and also drew a chart of the courses rivers take; using garrison records and registers from Tao, Huang, Gan, and Liang, together with distances broad and narrow and the hazards of mountains and sources of water, he compiled six fascicles of Separate Records and four of Records of the Western Frontier Rong, and submitted them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔賜幣馬珍器。

translations.literal: An edict granted silks, horses, and rare objects.
translations.idiomatic: An edict rewarded him with silks, horses, and precious objects.

sentences.zh: 又圖《海內華夷》，廣三丈，從三丈三尺，以寸為百里。

translations.literal: He also drew the Chart of Chinese and Barbarians Within the Seas, three zhang wide and three zhang three chi long, with one inch representing one hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: He also drew the Chart of Chinese and Barbarians Within the Seas, three zhang wide and three zhang three chi in length, using one inch to represent one hundred li.

sentences.zh: 並撰《古今郡國縣道四夷述》，其中國本之《禹貢》，外夷本班固《漢書》，古郡國題以墨，今州縣以朱，刊落疏舛，多所厘正。

translations.literal: He also compiled An Account of Commanderies, Counties, Roads, and the Four Barbarians, Ancient and Modern; for China he took the Yu Gong as foundation, for outer barbarians Ban Gu's Book of Han; ancient commanderies and states were titled in black, present prefectures and counties in red; he cut away errors and omissions and corrected much.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote An Account of Commanderies, Counties, Roads, and the Four Barbarians, Ancient and Modern, taking the Yu Gong as his foundation for China and Ban Gu's Book of Han for foreign peoples; ancient commanderies and states he marked in black, present prefectures and counties in red, pruning errors and correcting many mistakes.

sentences.zh: 帝善之，賜予加等。

translations.literal: The emperor approved and granted him an increased reward.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his work and granted him an enhanced reward.

sentences.zh: 或指圖問其邦人，咸得其真。

translations.literal: If one pointed on the map and asked a man of that state, all obtained the truth.
translations.idiomatic: If one pointed on the map and questioned a native of that region, the answers were invariably accurate.

sentences.zh: 又著《貞元十道錄》，以貞觀分天下隸十道，在景雲為按察，開元為采訪，廢置升降備焉。

translations.literal: He also wrote Records of the Ten Circuits in the Zhenyuan Era, taking Zhenguan's division of the realm into ten circuits; under Jingyun they became surveillance commissions, under Kaiyuan investigation commissioners—all abolitions, establishments, promotions, and demotions fully recorded.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Records of the Ten Circuits in the Zhenyuan Era, based on the Zhenguan division of the empire into ten circuits; under Jingyun they became surveillance commissions and under Kaiyuan investigation commissioners, with every abolition, establishment, promotion, and demotion fully recorded.

sentences.zh: 至陰陽雜數罔不通。

translations.literal: As for yin-yang lore and miscellaneous numerology, none was unknown to him.
translations.idiomatic: As for yin-yang lore and miscellaneous numerology, there was none he did not understand.

sentences.zh: 其器恢然，蓋長者也，不喜臧否人物。

translations.literal: His bearing was broad and magnanimous; he was in essence a man of long view and did not like to praise or blame people.
translations.idiomatic: His bearing was broad and magnanimous; he was fundamentally a man of long view and did not care to pass judgment on others.

sentences.zh: 為相十三年，雖安危大事亡所發明，而檢身厲行，自其所長。

translations.literal: As chief minister for thirteen years, though on great matters of safety and peril he originated nothing, in restraining himself and enforcing conduct he did what he did best.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister for thirteen years, though he originated nothing on great matters of national safety and peril, in personal discipline and rigorous conduct he excelled in his own way.

sentences.zh: 每歸第，對賓客無少倦，家人近習，不見其喜慍。

translations.literal: Whenever he returned home he entertained guests without the least weariness; family and close attendants never saw him pleased or angry.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he returned home he entertained guests without the least sign of weariness; family and close attendants never saw him show pleasure or anger.

sentences.zh: 世謂淳德有常者。

translations.literal: The age called him a man of pure virtue and constancy.
translations.idiomatic: His contemporaries regarded him as a man of pure and steadfast virtue.

sentences.zh: =杜佑=

translations.literal: = Du You =
translations.idiomatic: = Du You =

sentences.zh: 杜佑，字君卿，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Du You, courtesy name Junqing, was a man of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Du You, whose courtesy name was Junqing, came from Wannian in the capital district of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 父希望，重然諾，所交遊皆一時俊傑。

translations.literal: His father Xiwang valued promises heavily; those he befriended were all outstanding men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiwang placed great weight on keeping his word; everyone he befriended was a leading figure of the day.

sentences.zh: 為安陵令，都督宋慶禮表其異政。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Anling, Governor Song Qingli memorialized his exceptional administration.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as magistrate of Anling, Governor Song Qingli memorialized his exceptional governance.

sentences.zh: 坐小累去官。

translations.literal: He was removed from office on a minor charge.
translations.idiomatic: He left office after a minor infraction.

sentences.zh: 開元中，交河公主嫁突騎施，詔希望為和親判官。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era Princess Jiaohe married the Turgesh; an edict appointed Xiwang marriage-alliance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan reign Princess Jiaohe was married to the Turgesh, and an edict appointed Xiwang commissioner for the marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 信安郡王漪表署靈州別駕、關內道度支判官。

translations.literal: Prince of Xin'an Jun Yi memorialized him as Vice-Prefect of Lingzhou and fiscal commissioner adjutant for Guannei circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xin'an Jun Yi recommended him as vice-prefect of Lingzhou and adjutant for fiscal affairs on the Guannei circuit.

sentences.zh: 自代州都督召還京師，對邊事，玄宗才之。

translations.literal: Summoned back to the capital from his post as Governor of Daizhou, he answered on frontier affairs and Emperor Xuanzong recognized his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to the capital from his post as governor of Daizhou, he answered questions on frontier affairs and Emperor Xuanzong recognized his ability.

sentences.zh: 屬吐蕃攻勃律，勃律乞歸，右相李林甫方領隴西節度，故拜希望鄯州都督，知留後。

translations.literal: When Tibet attacked Bolor and Bolor sought to submit, Chief Minister Li Linfu was then holding the Longxi command, so Xiwang was appointed Governor of Shanzhou with acting authority.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibet attacked Bolor and Bolor sought to submit, Chief Minister Li Linfu was then in charge of the Longxi command, so Xiwang was appointed governor of Shanzhou with acting authority.

sentences.zh: 馳傳度隴，破烏莽眾，斬千餘級，進拔新城，振旅而還。

translations.literal: He rode post-haste across Long, defeated the Wumang host, beheaded more than a thousand, advanced to seize Xincheng, and returned with his army in good order.
translations.idiomatic: He rode post-haste across Long, defeated the Wumang forces, beheaded more than a thousand men, advanced to capture Xincheng, and returned with his army in good order.

sentences.zh: 擢鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Court for Diplomatic Relations.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of the Court for Diplomatic Relations.

sentences.zh: 於是置鎮西軍，希望引師部分塞下，吐蕃懼，遺書求和。

translations.literal: The Western Garrison Army was then established; Xiwang led troops to divide and block below the passes; Tibet was afraid and sent a letter seeking peace.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Garrison Army was then established; Xiwang led troops to divide and block the passes below, and Tibet, alarmed, sent a letter seeking peace.

sentences.zh: 希望報曰：「受和非臣下所得專。」

translations.literal: Xiwang replied: "Accepting peace is not something a subject may decide on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Xiwang replied, "Accepting peace is not something a subject may decide on his own.

sentences.zh: 虜悉眾爭檀泉，希望大小戰數十，俘其大酋，至莫門，焚積蓄，卒城而還。

translations.literal: The barbarians mustered all their forces to contest Tanquan; Xiwang fought great and small battles several tens of times, captured their great chief, reached Momen, burned their stores, completed the fortifications, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy mustered all their forces to contest Tanquan; Xiwang fought dozens of engagements large and small, captured their great chief, reached Momen, burned their stores, completed the fortifications, and returned.

sentences.zh: 授二子官。

translations.literal: His two sons were granted offices.
translations.idiomatic: His two sons were granted official posts.

sentences.zh: 時軍屢興，府庫虛寡，希望居數歲，芻粟金帛豐余。

translations.literal: At the time campaigns were frequent and the treasury empty and thin; in several years under Xiwang fodder, grain, gold, and silks were abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigns were frequent at the time and the treasury was empty and depleted; after several years under Xiwang, fodder, grain, gold, and silks were in surplus.

sentences.zh: 宦者牛仙童行邊，或勸希望結其，答曰：「以貨藩身，吾不忍。」

translations.literal: Eunuch Niu Xiantong toured the frontier; some urged Xiwang to curry favor with him, and he replied: "To buy my safety with goods—I cannot bear it.
translations.idiomatic: When the eunuch Niu Xiantong toured the frontier, some urged Xiwang to win him over with gifts, but he replied, "To buy my safety with goods—I cannot bear it.

sentences.zh: 仙童還奏希望不職，下遷恒州刺史，徙西河。

translations.literal: Xiantong returned and reported that Xiwang was derelict; he was demoted to Prefect of Hengzhou and transferred to Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: Xiantong returned and reported that Xiwang was derelict in duty; he was demoted to prefect of Hengzhou and transferred to Xihe.

sentences.zh: 而仙童受諸將金事泄，抵死，畀金者皆得罪。

translations.literal: But when Xiantong's acceptance of gold from the generals was exposed, he was put to death, and all who had given gold were punished.
translations.idiomatic: But when it was revealed that Xiantong had accepted gold from the generals, he was put to death, and all who had given him gold were punished.

sentences.zh: 希望愛重文學，門下所引如崔顥等皆名重當時。

translations.literal: Xiwang loved and valued literature; those he brought in, such as Cui Hao, were all famous and weighty in their day.
translations.idiomatic: Xiwang loved and valued literature; those he brought into his service, such as Cui Hao, were all celebrated figures of the age.

sentences.zh: 佑以蔭補濟南參軍事、剡縣丞。

translations.literal: You entered office by yin privilege as Jinan military adjutant and Shan county assistant magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: You entered office through yin privilege as military adjutant of Jinan and assistant magistrate of Shan county.

sentences.zh: 嘗過潤州刺史韋元甫，元甫以故人子待之，不加禮。

translations.literal: Once he passed by Runzhou Prefect Wei Yuanfu; Yuanfu treated him as a son of an old friend and did not extend special courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Once he visited Runzhou prefect Wei Yuanfu, who treated him merely as the son of an old acquaintance and showed him no special courtesy.

sentences.zh: 它日，元甫有疑獄不能決，試訊佑，佑為辨處，契要無不盡。

translations.literal: Another day Yuanfu had a doubtful case he could not decide and tried questioning You; You analyzed and disposed of it, and every essential point was fully covered.
translations.idiomatic: On another day Yuanfu had a doubtful legal case he could not resolve and tried questioning You; You analyzed and disposed of it, covering every essential point without omission.

sentences.zh: 元甫奇之，署司法參軍，府徙浙西、淮南，表置幕府。

translations.literal: Yuanfu marveled at him and appointed him judicial adjutant; when the prefecture moved to Zhexi and Huainan, he memorialized to place him on the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfu was astonished and appointed him judicial adjutant; when the prefecture was transferred to Zhexi and Huainan, he memorialized to place You on his staff.

sentences.zh: 入為工部郎中，充江淮青苗使，再遷容管經略使。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Bureau Director in the Ministry of Works, served as Jianghuai green-sprout commissioner, and was promoted again to Rongguan frontier commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as a bureau director in the Ministry of Works, served as green-sprout commissioner for the Jianghuai region, and was promoted again to frontier commissioner of Rongguan.

sentences.zh: 楊炎輔政，歷金部郎中，為水陸轉運使，改度支兼和糴使。

translations.literal: When Yang Yan assisted in government, he passed through Bureau Director of the Revenue Section, became Commissioner for Water and Land Transport, and was changed to Director of the Treasury with concurrent Commissioner for Harmonious Purchase.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Yan came to power, You served as bureau director of the Revenue Section, then as commissioner for water and land transport, and was reassigned as director of the treasury with concurrent commissioner for government grain purchases.

sentences.zh: 於是軍興饋漕，佑得剸決。

translations.literal: At this time with the army raised and supplies transported, You was able to decide and cut through.
translations.idiomatic: With the army mobilized and supply transport under way, You proved able to decide matters swiftly and decisively.

sentences.zh: 以戶部侍郎判度支。

translations.literal: As Vice Minister of Revenue he concurrently directed the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice minister of revenue with concurrent authority over the treasury.

sentences.zh: 建中初，河朔兵挐戰，民困，賦無所出。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong the Hebei-Shuo armies grappled in battle; the people were distressed and levies had nowhere to come from.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era the armies of Hebei and Shuo fought one another; the people were in distress and taxes could not be collected.

sentences.zh: 佑以為救敝莫若省用，省用則省官，乃上議曰：

translations.literal: You held that to rescue exhaustion nothing was better than reducing expenditure; reducing expenditure meant reducing officials, and so he submitted a proposal saying:
translations.idiomatic: You held that to relieve distress nothing was better than cutting expenditure, and cutting expenditure meant reducing officials; he therefore submitted a proposal saying:

sentences.zh: 漢光武建武中廢縣四百，吏率十署一；

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu of Han in the Jianwu era abolished four hundred counties, with one official for every ten offices;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu of Han, in the Jianwu era, abolished four hundred counties and reduced officials to roughly one for every ten posts;

sentences.zh: 魏太和時分遣使者省吏員，正始時並郡縣；

translations.literal: in Wei under Taihe commissioners were sent out to reduce the number of clerks; under Zhengshi commanderies and counties were merged;
translations.idiomatic: under Wei in the Taihe era commissioners were sent out to reduce the number of clerks, and under Zhengshi commanderies and counties were merged;

sentences.zh: 晉太元省官七百；

translations.literal: in Jin under Taixuan seven hundred offices were cut;
translations.idiomatic: under Jin in the Taixuan era seven hundred offices were cut;

sentences.zh: 隋開皇廢郡五百；

translations.literal: in Sui under Kaihuang five hundred commanderies were abolished;
translations.idiomatic: under Sui in the Kaihuang era five hundred commanderies were abolished;

sentences.zh: 貞觀初省內官六百員。

translations.literal: at the beginning of Zhenguan six hundred inner offices were cut.
translations.idiomatic: and at the beginning of Zhenguan six hundred inner offices were cut.

sentences.zh: 設官之本，以治眾庶，故古者計人置吏，不肯虛設。

translations.literal: The root of establishing offices is to govern the multitude; thus in antiquity they counted people to set clerks and would not establish them in vain.
translations.idiomatic: The purpose of establishing offices is to govern the people; in antiquity they counted the population to determine how many clerks to appoint and would not create posts needlessly.

sentences.zh: 自漢至唐，因征戰艱難以省吏員，誠救弊之切也。

translations.literal: From Han to Tang, because of the hardships of campaigns they reduced clerks—truly the urgent remedy for exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: From Han through Tang, in times of the hardships of war they reduced the number of clerks—truly the most urgent remedy for distress.

sentences.zh: 昔咎繇作士，今刑部尚書、大理卿，則二咎繇也。

translations.literal: In antiquity Gao Yao was Minister of Crime; today the Minister of Justice and the Chief Judge of Dali—there are two Gao Yaos.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Gao Yao served as minister of crime; today the Minister of Justice and the chief judge of Dali make two Gao Yaos.

sentences.zh: 垂作共工，今工部尚書、將作監，則二垂也。

translations.literal: Chui was Minister of Works; today the Minister of Works and the Director of Imperial Construction—there are two Chuis.
translations.idiomatic: Chui served as minister of works; today the Minister of Works and the director of imperial construction make two Chuis.

sentences.zh: 契作司徒，今司徒、戶部尚書，則二契也。

translations.literal: Qi was Minister of Education; today the Minister of Education and the Minister of Revenue—there are two Qis.
translations.idiomatic: Qi served as minister of education; today the Minister of Education and the Minister of Revenue make two Qis.

sentences.zh: 伯夷為秩宗，今禮部尚書、禮儀使，則二伯夷也。

translations.literal: Bo Yi was Director of Rites; today the Minister of Rites and the Commissioner of Ceremonies—there are two Bo Yis.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Yi served as director of rites; today the Minister of Rites and the commissioner of ceremonies make two Bo Yis.

sentences.zh: 伯益為虞，今虞部郎中、都水使司，則二伯益也。

translations.literal: Bo Yi was Director of Forestry; today the Bureau Director of Forestry and the Commissioner of Waterways—there are two Bo Yis.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Yi served as director of forestry; today the bureau director of forestry and the commissioner of waterways make two Bo Yis.

sentences.zh: 伯冏為太僕，今太僕卿、駕部郎中、尚輦奉御、閑廄使，則四伯冏也。

translations.literal: Bo Jiong was Grand Master of the Stud; today the Grand Master of the Stud, Bureau Director of the Imperial Carriage, Palace Attendant of the Imperial Carriage, and Commissioner of the Pasture Stud—there are four Bo Jiongs.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Jiong served as grand master of the stud; today the grand master of the stud, the bureau director of the imperial carriage, the palace attendant of the imperial carriage, and the commissioner of the pasture stud make four Bo Jiongs.

sentences.zh: 古天子有六軍，漢前後左右將軍四人，今十二衛、神策八軍，凡將軍六十員。

translations.literal: The ancient Son of Heaven had six armies; Han had four generals—Front, Rear, Left, and Right; today the Twelve Guards and the Eight Divine Strategy Armies—in all sixty generalships.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient Son of Heaven had six armies; Han had four generals of the front, rear, left, and right; today the Twelve Guards and the Eight Divine Strategy Armies account for sixty generalships in all.

sentences.zh: 舊名不廢，新資日加。

translations.literal: Old titles are not abolished, new stipends daily increase.
translations.idiomatic: Old titles are not abolished while new stipends are added day by day.

sentences.zh: 且漢置別駕，隨刺史巡察，猶今觀察使之有副也。

translations.literal: Moreover Han established Vice-Prefects to accompany prefects on inspection tours—like today's surveillance commissioners having deputies.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Han established vice-prefects to accompany prefects on inspection tours, much as today's surveillance commissioners have deputies.

sentences.zh: 參軍者，參其府軍事，猶今節度判官也。

translations.literal: A military adjutant participates in the commandery's military affairs—like today's circuit military judge.
translations.idiomatic: The post of military adjutant meant taking part in a prefecture's military affairs, much as today's circuit military judge does.

sentences.zh: 官名職務，直遷易不同爾，詎有事實哉？

translations.literal: Titles and duties merely changed with the times; how could there be any real difference?
translations.idiomatic: Office titles and duties had simply shifted with the times—what substantive difference could there be?

sentences.zh: 誠宜斟酌繁省。

translations.literal: It is truly fitting to weigh what is redundant against what may be cut.
translations.idiomatic: The court should seriously weigh what to keep and what to cut.

sentences.zh: 欲致治者先正名。

translations.literal: Whoever would bring order must first rectify names.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever seeks good government must first set names and offices right.

sentences.zh: 神龍中，官紀蕩然，有司大集選者，既無闕員，則置員外官二千人，自是以為常。

translations.literal: In the Shenlong era official discipline collapsed; the authorities massed candidates for selection, and with no vacant posts they created two thousand supernumerary officials—thereafter taken as routine.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenlong era official discipline collapsed; when the authorities gathered candidates for appointment and found no vacancies, they created two thousand supernumerary posts, and that practice then became routine.

sentences.zh: 當開元、天寶中，四方無虞，編戶九百餘萬，帑藏豐溢，雖有浮費，不足為憂。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras the four quarters were untroubled, registered households exceeded nine million, and the treasury overflowed; though there was waste, it was no cause for worry.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kaiyuan and Tianbao the realm was at peace, registered households stood above nine million, and the treasury was flush; even with some waste, there was little to fear.

sentences.zh: 今黎苗雕瘵，天下戶百三十萬，陛下詔使者按比，才得三百萬，比天寶三分之一，就中浮寄又五之二，出賦者已耗，而食之者如舊，安可不革？

translations.literal: Now the common people are wasted and afflicted; household registers in the realm show only 1.3 million, yet when Your Majesty ordered envoys to verify and compare, only three million were found—one third of the Tianbao figure; of these, two fifths were fictitious entries. Those who pay taxes are already exhausted while those who consume revenue remain as before—how can this not be reformed?
translations.idiomatic: Today the people are worn down and sickly; the books list only 1.3 million households empire-wide, yet when Your Majesty sent officials to check and compare, they found only three million—one third of the Tianbao count—and two fifths of even that were fictitious registrations. The taxpayers are drained while the eaters of public grain are as numerous as ever. How can this go unreformed?

sentences.zh: 議者以天下尚有跋扈不廷，一省官吏，被罷者皆往托焉。

translations.literal: Critics said that the realm still had arrogant men who would not attend court, and that if one province cut officials, all who were dismissed would go and attach themselves to such men.
translations.idiomatic: Some argued that unruly warlords still defied the court, and that officials cut from one province would simply flock to them for patronage.

sentences.zh: 此常情之說，類非至論。

translations.literal: This is the language of ordinary sentiment and is broadly not the ultimate argument.
translations.idiomatic: That is ordinary talk, not serious policy.

sentences.zh: 且才者薦用，不才者何患其亡，又況顧姻戚家產哉！

translations.literal: Moreover the talented are recommended and employed—why fear the loss of the untalented? Still less need one worry over in-laws and family property!
translations.idiomatic: Besides, men of talent are recommended and used—why worry about losing the incompetent? And why fret over their kin or estates?

sentences.zh: 建武時公孫述、隗囂未滅，太和、正始、太元時吳、蜀鼎立，開皇時陳尚割據，皆羅取俊乂，猶不慮失人以資敵。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu era Gongsun Shu and Wei Xiao were not yet destroyed; in the Taihe, Zhengshi, and Taiyuan eras Wu and Shu stood in tripartite division; in the Kaihuang era Chen still held a separate domain—all gathered outstanding men and still did not fear losing people to supply the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jianwu, Gongsun Shu and Wei Xiao had not yet fallen; in the Taihe, Zhengshi, and Taiyuan reigns Wu and Shu still divided the realm; under Kaihuang Chen still held out—all those states recruited the able and never worried that trimming offices would arm their foes.

sentences.zh: 今田悅輩繁刑暴賦，惟軍是恤，遇士人如奴，固無范睢業秦、賈季強狄之患。

translations.literal: Today men like Tian Yue impose frequent punishments and violent levies, caring only for the army, and treat scholars like slaves—so there is truly no danger of a Fan Ju serving Qin or a Jia Ji strengthening the Di.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Tian Yue rule by harsh law and crushing taxes, think only of their armies, and treat literati like slaves—there is no real risk of a Fan Ju defecting to Qin or a Jia Ji strengthening a foreign power.

sentences.zh: 若以習久不可以遽改，且應權省別駕、參軍、司馬，州縣額內官，約戶置尉。

translations.literal: If because custom is long-standing it cannot be changed at once, then for the time being one should provisionally cut vice-prefects, adjutants, and military aides, fill county and prefecture quotas within the authorized numbers, and set constables in proportion to households.
translations.idiomatic: If long custom cannot be overturned overnight, at least provisionally eliminate vice-prefects, adjutants, and military aides, keep prefectural and county staffs within authorized quotas, and appoint constables according to household counts.

sentences.zh: 當罷者，有行義，在所以聞；

translations.literal: Those to be dismissed should have conduct and righteousness known in their locality;
translations.idiomatic: Those slated for dismissal should be men whose conduct and integrity are known where they serve;

sentences.zh: 不如狀，舉者當坐；

translations.literal: if they do not match the report, the recommender shall be punished;
translations.idiomatic: if they fail to match their recommendation, the recommender should be punished;

sentences.zh: 不為人舉者，任參常調。

translations.literal: those whom no one recommends shall be assigned to ordinary serial appointments.
translations.idiomatic: and those whom no one will recommend should be left to ordinary routine appointments.

sentences.zh: 亦何患哉？

translations.literal: What is there to worry about?
translations.idiomatic: What harm could that do?

sentences.zh: 如魏置柱國，當時宿德盛業者居之，貴寵第一；

translations.literal: For example, when Wei established the Pillar of State, men of long-standing virtue and great achievement held it and ranked first in honor and favor;
translations.idiomatic: When Wei created the rank of Pillar of State, only men of long-standing virtue and great achievement held it, and they stood first in honor and favor;

sentences.zh: 周、隋間授受已多，國家以為勛級，才得地三十頃耳。

translations.literal: between Zhou and Sui the appointments had already grown numerous, and the state made it a merit grade yielding only thirty qing of land.
translations.idiomatic: but between Zhou and Sui the title had been handed out so often that the dynasty treated it merely as a merit grade worth only thirty qing of land.

sentences.zh: 又開府儀同三司、光祿大夫，亦官名，以其太多，回作階級。

translations.literal: Again, Grand Preceptor of State with the Three Insignia and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness were also office titles; because there were too many holders, they were turned into rank grades.
translations.idiomatic: Likewise Grand Preceptor of State with the Three Insignia and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness were real offices; when holders grew too numerous, they were reduced to rank grades.

sentences.zh: 隨時立制，遇弊則變，何必因循憚改作耶？

translations.literal: Institutions should be established according to the times; when abuses appear, change them—why cling to precedent and fear reform?
translations.idiomatic: Institutions should be made for their time; when abuse appears, change them—why cling to precedent and dread reform?

sentences.zh: 議入，不省。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; the Emperor took no notice.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went in, and the emperor ignored it.

sentences.zh: 盧杞當國，惡之，出為蘇州刺史。

translations.literal: When Lu Qi held power he hated You and had him sent out as Prefect of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi, who then dominated the government, disliked him and had him posted out as prefect of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 前刺史母喪解，佑母在，辭不行，改饒州。

translations.literal: The previous prefect had left on account of his mother's mourning; You's mother was still living, so he declined the post and was reassigned to Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The outgoing prefect had left because of his mother's mourning; since You's mother was still alive, he declined the appointment and was transferred to Raozhou instead.

sentences.zh: 俄遷嶺南節度使。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to military governor of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made military governor of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 佑為開大衢，疏析廛闬，以息火災。

translations.literal: You opened broad avenues, cleared and divided lanes and market wards, and thereby checked fires.
translations.idiomatic: He opened wide streets, cleared and divided lanes and market wards, and thereby reduced the danger of fire.

sentences.zh: 朱厓黎民三世保險不賓，佑討平之。

translations.literal: The people of Zhuya and Li had for three generations held difficult terrain and would not submit; You campaigned and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: The peoples of Zhuya and Li had for three generations held difficult country and refused submission; You campaigned and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 召拜尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and appointed vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 俄出為淮南節度使，以母喪解，詔不許。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as military governor of Huainan; he sought release on account of his mother's mourning, but an edict would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was posted as military governor of Huainan; when he asked to leave office for his mother's mourning, the throne refused.

sentences.zh: 徐州節度使張建封卒，軍亂，立其子愔，請於朝，帝不許，乃詔佑檢校尚書左僕射、同中書門下平章事，節度徐泗討定之。

translations.literal: When Xuzhou military governor Zhang Jianfeng died the army rebelled, enthroned his son Yin, and petitioned the court; the Emperor did not approve, and then ordered You as acting Minister of the Left, Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs, to hold the Xu-Si command and settle the affair.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jianfeng, military governor of Xuzhou, died, the army mutinied and set up his son Yin, then petitioned the court for approval. The emperor refused, and ordered You—now acting minister of the left and associate director of the Department of State Affairs—to take the Xu-Si command and put the rebellion down.

sentences.zh: 佑具舠艦，遣屬將孟準度淮擊徐，不克，引還。

translations.literal: You prepared light warships and sent his subordinate general Meng Huai to cross the Huai and strike Xuzhou; he did not overcome them and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: You fitted out light warships and sent his subordinate Meng Huai across the Huai to attack Xuzhou, but the assault failed and the force withdrew.

sentences.zh: 佑於出師應變非所長，因固境不敢進，乃招授愔徐州節度使，析濠、泗二州隸淮南。

translations.literal: You was not skilled at adapting on campaign; he therefore held his borders and dared not advance, then negotiated and appointed Yin military governor of Xuzhou, while Hao and Si prefectures were detached to Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign improvisation was not You's strength; he held his lines and dared not advance, then negotiated Yin into the Xuzhou command and detached the Hao and Si prefectures to Huainan.

sentences.zh: 初，佑決雷陂以廣灌溉，斥海瀕棄地為田，積米至五十萬斛，列營三十區，士馬整飭，四鄰畏之；

translations.literal: Earlier You had opened the Leibo reservoir to broaden irrigation, reclaimed abandoned land along the seashore for fields, accumulated grain to five hundred thousand hu, arrayed camps in thirty districts, and kept troops and horses in good order so that the neighboring circuits feared him;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier he had breached the Leibo reservoir to expand irrigation, reclaimed coastal wasteland for fields, stockpiled grain to five hundred thousand hu, laid out thirty camp districts, and kept soldiers and horses in good order so that neighboring circuits feared him;

sentences.zh: 然寬假僚佐，故南宮僔、李亞、鄭元均至爭權亂政，帝為佑斥去之。

translations.literal: yet he was lenient with his staff, so Nangong Pu, Li Ya, and Zheng Yuanjun came to contend for power and disorder government; the Emperor dismissed them on You's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: yet he was indulgent toward his staff, so Nangong Pu, Li Ya, and Zheng Yuanjun fought for power and threw the administration into disorder, and the emperor removed them for his sake.

sentences.zh: 十九年，拜檢校司空、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was appointed acting Minister of Works and Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was made acting minister of works and associate director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 德宗崩，詔攝冢宰。

translations.literal: When Dezong died, an edict ordered You to act as steward of the royal corpse.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong died, an edict named You steward of the royal corpse.

sentences.zh: 進檢校司徒，兼度支鹽鐵使。

translations.literal: He was advanced to acting Minister of Education and concurrently Commissioner of Revenue and Salt and Iron.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting minister of education and made concurrent commissioner of revenue and of the salt and iron monopolies.

sentences.zh: 於是王叔文為副，佑既以宰相不親事，叔文遂專權。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Shuwen served as his deputy; since You as chief minister did not attend to affairs in person, Shuwen came to monopolize power.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shuwen then served as his deputy; because You as chief minister no longer handled affairs himself, Shuwen seized sole control.

sentences.zh: 後叔文以母喪還第，佑有所按決，郎中陳諫請須叔文，佑曰：「使不可專耶？」

translations.literal: Later, when Shuwen returned home on his mother's mourning, You undertook some investigations and decisions; Bureau Director Chen Jian asked that Shuwen be consulted, and You said, "May the commissioner not act on his own?"
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Shuwen went home for his mother's mourning, You took up certain investigations and rulings; bureau director Chen Jian asked that Shuwen be consulted, and You said, "May the commissioner not decide on his own?"

sentences.zh: 乃出諫為河中少尹。

translations.literal: He then transferred Jian to Vice-Governor of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: He then transferred Chen Jian out as vice-governor of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 叔文欲搖東宮，冀佑為助，佑不應，乃謀逐之，未決而敗。

translations.literal: Shuwen wished to shake the Eastern Palace and hoped You would help; You did not respond, so Shuwen plotted to drive him out, but before the plan was settled it failed.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen tried to undermine the crown prince and hoped for You's support; You would not answer, so Shuwen plotted to remove him, but the plot collapsed before it was carried out.

sentences.zh: 佑更薦李巽以自副。

translations.literal: You then recommended Li Xun as his own deputy.
translations.idiomatic: You then recommended Li Xun as his deputy in place of Shuwen.

sentences.zh: 憲宗在諒暗，復攝冢宰，盡讓度支鹽鐵於巽。

translations.literal: When Xianzong was in the mourning shed, You again acted as steward of the corpse and fully yielded the revenue and salt-and-iron offices to Xun.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Xianzong was still in mourning seclusion, You again served as steward of the corpse and handed the revenue and salt-and-iron offices entirely to Xun.

sentences.zh: 始，度支嗇，用度多，署吏權攝百司，繁而不綱；

translations.literal: At first the Revenue Bureau was tight-fisted while expenditures were heavy; its clerks by delegated authority took charge of the hundred offices—numerous but without coherence;
translations.idiomatic: At first the Revenue Bureau was tight-fisted while spending was heavy; its clerks by delegated authority ran the hundred offices—many hands with no clear thread;

sentences.zh: 佑以營繕還將作，木炭歸司農，湅染還少府，職務簡修。

translations.literal: You returned construction to the Directorate of Imperial Works, charcoal to the Directorate of Agriculture, dyeing and finishing to the Directorate of Palace Manufactories, and duties were simplified and put in order.
translations.idiomatic: You returned construction to the Directorate of Imperial Works, charcoal to the Directorate of Agriculture, dyeing and finishing to the Directorate of Palace Manufactories, and simplified duties into good order.

sentences.zh: 明年，拜司徒，封岐國公。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Minister of Education and enfeoffed Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed minister of education and enfeoffed as Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 党項陰導吐蕃為亂，諸將邀功，請討之。

translations.literal: The Tangut secretly guided Tibet into rebellion; the generals, seeking merit, asked to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut secretly incited Tibet to revolt; generals eager for glory asked permission to attack.

sentences.zh: 佑以為無良邊臣，有為而叛，即上疏曰：

translations.literal: You held that there were no good frontier officials, that rebellion arose because someone provoked it, and he submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: You believed the frontier lacked good officials and that rebellion had been provoked by their misconduct, and submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 昔周宣中興，獫狁為害，追之太原，及境而止，不欲弊中國，怒遠夷也。

translations.literal: Formerly, in King Xuan's restoration of Zhou, the Xianyun did harm; he pursued them to Taiyuan and stopped at the border, unwilling to exhaust the Middle Kingdom or provoke distant barbarians in anger.
translations.idiomatic: When King Xuan restored Zhou, the Xianyun raided; he pursued them to Taiyuan and halted at the border, unwilling to wear out the central states or provoke distant tribes in anger.

sentences.zh: 秦恃兵力，北拒匈奴，西逐諸羌，結怨階亂，實生謫戍。

translations.literal: Qin relied on military force, resisted the Xiongnu in the north and drove off the various Qiang in the west, heaped up enmity and step by step brought disorder, and in truth produced the exiles of the frontier garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Qin trusted force alone, held off the Xiongnu in the north and drove the Qiang tribes in the west, piled up hatred until disorder followed, and in the end bred the exiled frontier garrisons.

sentences.zh: 蓋聖王之治天下，惟欲綏靜生人，西至於流沙，東漸於海，在北與南，止存聲教，豈疲內而事外耶？

translations.literal: The sage king's governance of the realm seeks only to bring the living to peace and quiet; west to the Moving Sands, east to the sea, north and south—he keeps only his transforming influence. How could he weary the interior to serve the exterior?
translations.idiomatic: A sage king governs the realm only to settle and quiet the living; west to the Moving Sands, east to the sea, north and south he extends only civilizing influence. Why exhaust the interior to serve the frontier?

sentences.zh: 昔馮奉世矯詔斬莎車王，傳首京師，威震西域，宣帝議加爵土，蕭望之獨謂矯制違命，雖有功不可為法，恐後奉使者為國家生事夷狄。

translations.literal: Formerly Feng Fengshi, by forged edict, beheaded the king of Shache and sent his head to the capital; his prestige shook the Western Regions. Emperor Xuan considered adding noble territory, but Xiao Wangzhi alone said that forging an edict and disobeying orders, though it had merit, must not be made a precedent, lest later envoys create trouble with the barbarians on the state's account.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Feng Fengshi, acting on a forged edict, beheaded the king of Shache and sent his head to court, and his fame shook the Western Regions. Emperor Xuan thought to reward him with a fief, but Xiao Wangzhi alone argued that usurping command, however meritorious, must not become precedent, lest later envoys embroil the state with the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 比突厥默啜寇害中國，開元初，郝靈佺捕斬之，自謂功莫與二，宋璟慮邊臣由此邀功，但授郎將而已，繇是訖開元之盛，不復議邊，中國遂安。

translations.literal: When the Turk Mo-chuo harried China, in the early Kaiyuan era Hao Lingxian captured and beheaded him; he claimed that his merit was second to none. Song Jing feared that frontier officials would thereby seek merit, and granted him only the rank of court gentleman; from then until the height of Kaiyuan the frontier was no longer debated, and the Middle Kingdom was secure.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turk Mo-chuo ravaged China, in early Kaiyuan Hao Lingxian captured and killed him and boasted that no deed could surpass his. Song Jing feared frontier officers would chase such glory and made him only a court gentleman; from then until Kaiyuan's zenith the frontier was left undebated, and the realm stayed secure.

sentences.zh: 此成敗鑒戒之不遠也。

translations.literal: This is a mirror of success and failure not far removed.
translations.idiomatic: That lesson of success and failure lies close at hand.

sentences.zh: 党項小蕃，與中國雜處，間者邊將侵刻，利其善馬子女，斂求繇役，遂致叛亡，與北狄西戎相誘盜邊。

translations.literal: The Tangut are a small tribe living mixed among the Chinese; lately frontier generals have oppressed them, coveting their good horses, sons, and daughters, exacting corvée and levies, until they fled in rebellion and, with northern Di and western Rong, incite one another to raid the borders.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut are a small people intermingled with the Chinese; lately frontier generals have squeezed them, coveting their fine horses and their sons and daughters, piling on labor and levies until they fled into rebellion and, with northern Di and western Rong, lure one another into border raids.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「遠人不服，則修文德以來之。」

translations.literal: The Documents say: "When distant peoples do not submit, then cultivate civil virtue to draw them in."
translations.idiomatic: The Documents say, "When distant peoples do not submit, cultivate civil virtue to win them.

sentences.zh: 管仲有言：「國家無使勇猛者為邊境。」

translations.literal: Guan Zhong said: "Let the state not place fierce and valiant men on the frontier."
translations.idiomatic: Guan Zhong said, "A state should not station fierce and valiant men on its borders."

sentences.zh: 此誠聖哲識微知著之略也。

translations.literal: This is truly the sage's strategy of discerning the subtle and knowing what is to come.
translations.idiomatic: That is the sage's way of reading the subtle and foreseeing what follows.

sentences.zh: 今戎醜方強，邊備未實，誠宜慎擇良將，使之完輯，禁絕誅求，示以信誠，來則懲禦，去則謹備。

translations.literal: Now the Rong are just growing strong and frontier defenses are not yet solid; it is truly fitting to choose good generals carefully, have them complete their defenses, forbid extortion, show sincerity and trust, punish when they come and guard carefully when they go.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Rong are growing strong and the frontier is not yet secure; the court should choose good generals carefully, have them complete their defenses, forbid extortion, show sincerity and good faith, punish arrivals and guard carefully when they withdraw.

sentences.zh: 彼當懷柔，革其奸謀。

translations.literal: They will then accept gentle handling and change their treacherous designs.
translations.idiomatic: They will accept gentle handling and abandon their plots.

sentences.zh: 何必亟興師役，坐取勞費哉？

translations.literal: Why must you hastily raise armies and campaigns, sitting only to incur labor and expense?
translations.idiomatic: Why rush to raise armies and campaigns, only to sit in weariness and waste?

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the memorial and adopted it.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，乞致仕，不聽，詔三五日一入中書，平章政事。

translations.literal: After more than a year he begged to retire; the court would not listen, and ordered him to enter the Secretariat every three to five days to deliberate on state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he asked to retire; the throne refused, but ordered him to enter the Secretariat every three to five days to deliberate on affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 佑每進見，天子尊禮之，官而不名。

translations.literal: Whenever You came to audience the Son of Heaven honored him with ritual and addressed him by office, not by personal name.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he came to audience the emperor honored him with full ceremony and addressed him by title rather than by name.

sentences.zh: 後數年，固乞骸骨，帝不得已，許之。

translations.literal: Several years later he firmly begged to leave his bones; the Emperor had no choice and granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Some years later he pressed again to retire for good; the emperor, unable to refuse further, allowed it.

sentences.zh: 仍拜光祿大夫、守太保致仕，俾朝朔望，遣中人錫予備厚。

translations.literal: He was still appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and retired as Guardian Grand Master, attending court on the first and fifteenth of the month; palace envoys were sent with lavish gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He was still made grand master of splendid happiness and retired as guardian grand master, attending court on the first and fifteenth of each month while palace envoys sent him lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 元和七年卒，年七十八，冊贈太傅，謚曰安簡。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yuanhe he died at seventy-eight; he was posthumously enfeoffed Grand Tutor and given the posthumous title Anjian.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yuanhe he died at seventy-eight; the court posthumously enfeoffed him grand tutor and gave him the posthumous title Anjian.

sentences.zh: 佑資嗜學，雖貴猶夜分讀書。

translations.literal: You by nature loved learning; though exalted he still read books far into the night.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning by nature; even after he rose high in office he still read far into the night.

sentences.zh: 先是，劉秩摭百家，侔周六官法，為《政典》三十五篇，房琯稱才過劉向。

translations.literal: Earlier Liu Zhi gathered the hundred schools and, matching the Six Offices of Zhou, composed thirty-five chapters of the Administrative Canon; Fang Guan said his talent surpassed Liu Xiang's.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Liu Zhi had drawn on the hundred schools and, paralleling the Zhou model of six offices, written thirty-five chapters of the Administrative Canon; Fang Guan said his talent surpassed Liu Xiang's.

sentences.zh: 佑以為未盡，因廣其闕，參益新禮，為二百篇，自號《通典》，奏之，優詔嘉美，儒者服其書約而詳。

translations.literal: You held that it was not complete; he therefore broadened its omissions, added new ritual material, and made two hundred chapters, titling it himself the Comprehensive Institutions; when he presented it an excellent edict praised it, and Confucian scholars admired the book as concise yet thorough.
translations.idiomatic: You judged the work incomplete, broadened its gaps, added new ritual material, and produced two hundred chapters under the title Comprehensive Institutions; when he presented it the throne answered with a warm edict of praise, and scholars admired the book as concise yet thorough.

sentences.zh: 為人平易遜順，與物不違忤，人皆愛重之，方漢胡廣，然練達文采不及也。

translations.literal: As a man he was easy and yielding, not at odds with others; all loved and esteemed him, and he was compared to Hu Guang of Han—yet he did not match Hu in practical mastery and literary polish.
translations.idiomatic: In person he was mild and accommodating, never at odds with others; everyone loved and respected him, and men compared him to Hu Guang of Han—though he lacked Hu's seasoned mastery and literary finish.

sentences.zh: 朱坡樊川，頗治亭觀林，鑿山股泉，與賓客置酒為樂。

translations.literal: At Zhupo and Fanchuan he greatly developed pavilions, towers, woods, and gardens, cut channels through the mountain's thigh for springs, and with guests set out wine for pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: At his estates at Zhupo and Fanchuan he laid out pavilions, towers, woods, and gardens, cut mountain channels for springs, and with guests raised cups for pleasure.

sentences.zh: 子弟皆奉朝請，貴盛為一時冠。

translations.literal: His sons and younger kin all held court appointments; their splendor was the crown of the age.
translations.idiomatic: His sons and younger kin all held court appointments, and their eminence was unmatched in their day.

sentences.zh: 天性精於吏職，為治不察，數斡計賦，相民利病而上下之，議者稱佑治行無缺。

translations.literal: By nature he was skilled in the duties of office; in governing he was not finicky, repeatedly intervened in tax assessments, weighed the people's hardships and benefits and adjusted them up or down, and critics said that in administrative conduct You had no flaw.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he excelled at official business; in governing he was not finicky, repeatedly intervened in tax assessments, weighed the people's hardships and benefits and adjusted policy accordingly, and critics said his administrative record had no flaw.

sentences.zh: 惟晚年以妾為夫人，有所蔽雲。

translations.literal: Only in his later years did he make a concubine his wife, and he showed partiality—it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Only in his later years did he elevate a concubine to wife, and it is said he showed partiality.

sentences.zh: 子 式方式方，字考元，以蔭授揚州參軍事。

translations.literal: Son: Shifang. Shifang, courtesy name Kaoyuan, entered office by yin privilege as military adjutant of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shifang, courtesy name Kaoyuan, entered office through yin privilege as military adjutant of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 再遷太常寺主簿，考定音律，卿高郢稱之。

translations.literal: He was transferred twice to clerk in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, examined and fixed pitch and measure, and Director Gao Ying praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He rose twice to clerk in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, where he examined and fixed pitch and measure, and Director Gao Ying praised his work.

sentences.zh: 佑既相，出為昭應令，遷太僕卿。

translations.literal: After You became chief minister, Shifang was sent out as magistrate of Zhaoying and promoted to Director of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: After You became chief minister, Shifang was posted out as magistrate of Zhaoying and then promoted to director of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 子悰，尚公主。

translations.literal: His son Cong married a princess.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cong married an imperial princess.

sentences.zh: 式方以右戚，輒病不視事。

translations.literal: Because Shifang was a maternal relative by marriage, he repeatedly feigned illness and would not attend to duties.
translations.idiomatic: As a maternal relative by marriage, Shifang repeatedly pleaded illness and neglected his duties.

sentences.zh: 穆宗立，授桂管觀察使。

translations.literal: When Muzong took the throne, Shifang was appointed surveillance commissioner of Guiguan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong ascended the throne, Shifang was appointed surveillance commissioner of Guiguan.

sentences.zh: 弟從郁痼疾，躬為營方藥羞膳，及死，期而泣，世稱其篤行。

translations.literal: His younger brother Congyu suffered a chronic illness; Shifang personally prepared prescriptions, medicines, and fine foods; when Congyu died he mourned for the full term and wept—his age praised this as devoted conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Congyu suffered a chronic illness; Shifang personally prepared prescriptions, medicines, and fine foods, and when Congyu died he observed the full mourning period in tears—the age praised his devotion.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 式方弟 從郁從郁，元和初為左補闕，崔群等以宰相子為嫌，再徙秘書丞。

translations.literal: Shifang's younger brother: Congyu. Congyu, in the early Yuanhe era, was Left Remonstrator; Cui Qun and others, taking him for a chief minister's son, transferred him twice to secretary of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: Shifang's younger brother Congyu, in early Yuanhe, served as left remonstrator; Cui Qun and others, seeing him as a chief minister's son, twice moved him down to secretary of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 終駕部員外郎。

translations.literal: He ended as Vice Director in the Ministry of Tribute Carriages.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as vice director in the Ministry of Tribute Carriages.

sentences.zh: 子牧。

translations.literal: Son: Mu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Mu.

sentences.zh: 式方子 悰悰，字永裕，以門蔭三遷太子司議郎。

translations.literal: Shifang's son: Cong. Cong, courtesy name Yongyu, by family yin privilege rose through three promotions to secretary for remonstrance of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Shifang's son Cong, courtesy name Yongyu, through family yin privilege rose in three steps to secretary for remonstrance of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 權德輿為相，其婿翰林學士獨孤郁以嫌自白。

translations.literal: When Quan Deyu was chief minister, his son-in-law Hanlin Academician Dugu Yu declared himself on account of the relationship.
translations.idiomatic: When Quan Deyu was chief minister, his son-in-law, Hanlin academician Dugu Yu, disclosed the relationship on grounds of conflict of interest.

sentences.zh: 憲宗見郁文雅，嘆曰：「德輿有婿乃爾！」

translations.literal: The Emperor, seeing Yu's refinement, sighed and said, "Deyu has such a son-in-law!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, seeing Yu's refinement, sighed and said, "Deyu has such a son-in-law!

sentences.zh: 時岐陽公主，帝愛女。

translations.literal: At that time Princess Qiyang was the Emperor's beloved daughter.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Princess Qiyang was the emperor's beloved daughter.

sentences.zh: 舊制，選多戚裏將家，帝始詔宰相李吉甫擇大臣子，皆辭疾，唯悰以選召見麟德殿。

translations.literal: By old custom, choices fell mostly on maternal kin and generals' families; the Emperor for the first time ordered Chief Minister Li Jifu to choose among ministers' sons—all pleaded illness except Cong, who alone accepted selection and was summoned to audience in Linde Hall.
translations.idiomatic: By old custom matches fell chiefly to imperial kin and generals' sons; the emperor for the first time ordered Chief Minister Li Jifu to choose from ministers' sons—all pleaded illness except Cong, who alone accepted and was summoned to audience in Linde Hall.

sentences.zh: 禮成，授殿中少監、駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: When the rites were completed he was appointed Vice Director of the Palace Domestic Service and Commissioner of the Consort Horse.
translations.idiomatic: After the rites were completed he was appointed vice director of the Palace Domestic Service and commissioner of the consort horse.

sentences.zh: 太和初，由澧州刺史召為京兆尹，遷鳳翔忠武節度使。

translations.literal: In the early Taihe era he was summoned from Prefect of Li to be Governor of the Capital and then military governor of Fengxiang and Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: In early Taihe he was recalled from prefect of Li to governor of the capital, then made military governor of Fengxiang and Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 入為工部尚書，判度支。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Minister of Works with concurrent control of the Revenue Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as minister of works with concurrent control of the Revenue Bureau.

sentences.zh: 會公主薨，悰久不謝，文宗怪之。

translations.literal: When the princess died Cong long failed to attend court in thanks; Emperor Wenzong found it strange.
translations.idiomatic: When the princess died Cong long failed to attend court in thanksgiving audience, and Emperor Wenzong thought it odd.

sentences.zh: 戶部侍郎李玨曰：「比駙馬都尉皆為公主服斬衰三年，故悰不得謝。」

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Revenue Li Jue said, "Formerly all commissioners of the consort horse office wore the deepest mourning for princesses for three years, so Cong could not attend court."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Revenue Li Jue said, "Formerly all commissioners of the consort horse office wore the deepest mourning for princesses for three years, so Cong could not attend court.

sentences.zh: 帝矍然，始詔杖而期，著於令。

translations.literal: The Emperor started, and then ordered mourning with the staff and a fixed term, writing it into statute.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor started, then ordered mourning with the staff and a fixed term, and wrote the rule into law.

sentences.zh: 會昌初，為淮南節度使。

translations.literal: In the early Huichang era he was military governor of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: In early Huichang he was military governor of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 武宗詔揚州監軍取倡家女十七人進禁中，監軍請悰同選，又欲閱良家有姿相者，悰曰：「吾不奉詔而輒與，罪也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wuzong ordered the Yangzhou army supervisor to take seventeen singing-girls from a brothel into the palace; the supervisor asked Cong to choose with him and also wished to inspect respectable families for good looks, and Cong said, "If I act without obeying the edict, that is a crime."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wuzong ordered the Yangzhou army supervisor to take seventeen singing-girls from a brothel into the palace; the supervisor asked Cong to help select them and also wanted to inspect respectable families for good looks, and Cong said, "If I join you without obeying the edict, that is a crime.

sentences.zh: 監軍怒，表於帝。

translations.literal: The supervisor was enraged and memorialized the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The supervisor was furious and memorialized the throne against him.

sentences.zh: 帝以悰有大臣體，乃詔罷所進伎，有意倚悰為相矣。

translations.literal: The emperor, seeing that Cong had the bearing of a great minister, then ordered the entertainers he had presented dismissed, intending to rely on Cong as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Judging that Du Cong carried himself like a statesman of the first rank, the emperor ordered the performers Cong had sent withdrawn from court and began to lean toward making him chief minister.

sentences.zh: 逾年，召拜檢校尚書右僕射、同中書門下平章事，仍判度支。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he was summoned and appointed Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Associate Grand Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and still oversaw the finance commission.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was recalled to serve as acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and associate grand councilor, while continuing to head the finance commission.

sentences.zh: 劉稹平，進左僕射、兼門下侍郎。

translations.literal: When Liu Zhen was pacified, he was promoted to Left Vice Director and concurrent Chancellery Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: After the suppression of Liu Zhen's rebellion he was promoted to Left Vice Director and concurrent Chancellery Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以本官罷，出為劍南東川節度使，徙西川，復鎮淮南。

translations.literal: Before long, he was dismissed from those posts, sent out as military commissioner of Jiannan East Circuit, transferred to West Circuit, and again posted to Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he left those offices, was appointed military commissioner of eastern Jiannan, then transferred to the west and finally returned to hold Huainan once more.

sentences.zh: 時方旱，道路流亡藉藉，民至漉漕渠遺米自給，呼為「聖米」，取陂澤茭蒲實皆盡，悰更表以為祥。

translations.literal: At the time there was drought; refugees thronged the roads, and the people even strained leftover grain from the canal for subsistence, calling it "sacred rice"; they exhausted the seeds of sedges and rushes in ponds and marshes, and Cong further memorialized that this was auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: A drought was on. Refugees packed the highways; people sifted stray grain from the transport canal to survive and called it "sacred rice." When even pond and marsh sedges were picked bare, Cong still submitted a memorial treating the hardship as a good omen.

sentences.zh: 獄囚積數百千人，而荒湎宴適不能事。

translations.literal: Prisoners piled up by the hundreds and thousands, yet he was sunk in wine and feasting and could not attend to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds and thousands of prisoners crowded the jails, yet he drowned himself in banquets and wine and could not manage his duties.

sentences.zh: 罷，兼太子太傅，分司東都。

translations.literal: Dismissed, he was made concurrent Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and assigned to the eastern capital as a commissioner without portfolio.
translations.idiomatic: Removed from office, he received the concurrent title Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and was posted to the eastern capital in a nominal role.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，起為留守，復節度劍南西川。

translations.literal: After a year he was recalled to serve as garrison commander, and again took military command of Jiannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was reappointed garrison commander of the eastern capital and once more made military commissioner of western Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 召為右僕射，判度支，進兼門下侍郎同平章事。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Right Vice Director, oversaw the finance commission, and advanced to concurrent Chancellery Vice Minister and associate grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as Right Vice Director with charge of the finance commission, he was then promoted to concurrent Chancellery Vice Minister and associate grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 始，宣宗世，夔王以下五王處大明宮內院，而鄆王居十六宅。

translations.literal: At the beginning, in Xuanzong's reign, the five princes from the Prince of Kui downward dwelt in the inner court of Daming Palace, while the Prince of Yun lived in the Sixteen Mansions.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, under Xuanzong, the five princes beginning with the Prince of Kui had been lodged in Daming Palace's inner compound, while the Prince of Yun resided in the Sixteen Mansions.

sentences.zh: 帝大漸，樞密使王歸長、馬公儒等以遺詔立夔王，而左軍中尉王宗實等入殿中，以為歸長等矯詔，乃迎鄆王立之，是為懿宗。

translations.literal: When the emperor was near death, the commissioners Wang Guichang, Ma Gongru, and others, by the testamentary edict, enthroned the Prince of Kui; but the Left Army Commandant Wang Zongshi and others entered the hall, holding that Guichang and the rest had forged the edict, and so welcomed the Prince of Yun to the throne—this was Yizong.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor lay dying, Commissioners Wang Guichang and Ma Gongru tried to enthrone the Prince of Kui by testamentary edict. Left Army Commandant Wang Zongshi and his faction entered the palace, denounced the edict as forged, and installed the Prince of Yun instead—the man who became Emperor Yizong.

sentences.zh: 久之，遣樞密使楊慶詣中書，獨揖悰，它宰相畢諴、杜審權、蔣伸不敢進，乃授悰中人請帝監國奏，因諭悰劾大臣名不在者抵罪。

translations.literal: Long afterward, the commissioner Yang Qing was sent to the Secretariat-Chancellery; he bowed to Cong alone—the other chancellors Bi Yan, Du Shenquan, and Jiang Shen dared not enter—and then handed Cong the palace memorial requesting the emperor to supervise the state, and instructed Cong to impeach any great minister whose name was not on it.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later Commissioner Yang Qing came to the Secretariat-Chancellery, bowed to Du Cong alone while Bi Yan, Du Shenquan, and Jiang Shen hung back, and handed him a palace memorial asking the new emperor to assume regency. He then told Cong to indict every senior minister whose name was omitted from the list.

sentences.zh: 悰遽封授使者復命，謂慶曰：「上踐祚未久，君等秉權，以愛憎殺大臣，公屬禍無日矣。」

translations.literal: Cong at once sealed it and returned it with the envoy, saying to Qing, "The sovereign has just ascended; you hold power and kill great ministers according to likes and dislikes—you yourselves will meet disaster any day now."
translations.idiomatic: Cong immediately resealed the document and sent it back with the messenger, telling Qing, "The Son of Heaven has only just taken the throne. You wield power and slay ministers as whim dictates—disaster will find you soon enough."

sentences.zh: 慶色沮去，帝怒亦釋，大臣遂安。

translations.literal: Qing's color fell and he withdrew; the emperor's anger also subsided, and the great ministers were thereafter secure.
translations.idiomatic: Qing left crestfallen; the emperor's wrath cooled as well, and the senior ministers were left in peace.

sentences.zh: 未幾，冊拜司空，封邠國公，以檢校司徒為鳳翔、荊南節度使，加兼太傅。

translations.literal: Before long he was enfeoffed as Minister of Works and Duke of Bin, then sent out as acting Grand Mentor with military command of Fengxiang and Jingnan, and further made concurrent Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was created Minister of Works and Duke of Bin, then posted as acting Grand Mentor with military command over Fengxiang and Jingnan and the added title of Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 會黔南觀察使秦匡謀討蠻，兵敗，奔於悰，悰囚之，劾不能伏節，有詔斬之。

translations.literal: It happened that the observation commissioner of Qiannan, Qin Kuangmou, campaigned against the Man tribes and was defeated; he fled to Cong, who imprisoned him and impeached him for failing to die at his post—an edict ordered his execution.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiannan observation commissioner Qin Kuangmou marched against the southern tribes, suffered defeat, and fled to Cong's jurisdiction, Cong had him imprisoned and charged with dereliction. An edict condemned him to death.

sentences.zh: 悰不意其死，駭愕得疾卒，年八十，贈太師。

translations.literal: Cong had not expected his death; startled and stricken, he fell ill and died, aged eighty; he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Cong had not expected the sentence to be carried out. Shocked and undone, he took ill and died at eighty. He was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 葬日，詔宰相百官臨奠。

translations.literal: On the day of burial, an edict ordered the chancellors and all officials to attend the obsequies.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his burial the court ordered chancellors and officials to attend the rites.

sentences.zh: 悰於大議論往往有所合，然才不周用。

translations.literal: In great deliberations Cong often agreed with what was right, yet his talent was not equal to full use.
translations.idiomatic: On weighty questions of policy he often hit the mark, yet his abilities never quite matched the demands placed on him.

sentences.zh: 雖出入將相，而厚自奉養，未嘗薦進幽隱，佑之素風衰焉，故時號「禿角犀」。

translations.literal: Though he rose and fell as general and minister, he enriched himself lavishly and never recommended the obscure; You's plain style decayed in him, and so the age nicknamed him "bald-horned rhinoceros."
translations.idiomatic: Though he rose to general and minister, he pampered himself extravagantly and never lifted hidden talent into office. The frugal tradition of his grandfather Du You withered in him, and men called him the "bald-horned rhinoceros."

sentences.zh: 悰子 裔休子裔休，懿宗時歷翰林學士、給事中，坐事貶端州司馬。

translations.literal: Cong's son: Yi-Xiu. Yi-Xiu, in Yizong's time, served as Hanlin academician and chief drafting attendant; for an offense he was demoted to prefectural aide in Duanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cong's son Yi-Xiu served under Yizong as Hanlin academician and chief drafting attendant until an offense sent him down to prefectural aide in Duanzhou.

sentences.zh: 弟孺休，字休之。

translations.literal: His younger brother Ru-Xiu, courtesy name Xiuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Ru-Xiu, styled Xiuzhi.

sentences.zh: 累擢給事中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to chief drafting attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to chief drafting attendant.

sentences.zh: 大順初，錢镠遣弟銶率兵擊徐約於蘇州，破之，以海昌都將沈粲行刺史事，而昭宗更命孺休為之，以粲為制置指揮使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhun, Qian Liu sent his younger brother Qian with troops to attack Xu Yue at Suzhou, defeated him, and had the Haichang garrison commander Shen Can act as prefect; but Zhaozong reappointed Ru-Xiu to the post and made Can commander of the pacification headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dazhun era Qian Liu sent his brother Qian with an army against Xu Yue at Suzhou. After the victory he left Haichang garrison commander Shen Can in charge of the prefecture, but Emperor Zhaozong reassigned the post to Ru-Xiu and made Shen commander of the pacification headquarters.

sentences.zh: 镠不悅，密遣粲害焉。
