translations.idiomatic: Otherwise they will cross the Huai and Si, join Xuzhou's malcontents, and the disaster will spread.

sentences.zh: 綯懦緩不能用，又自以不奉詔，因曰：「彼不為暴，聽其度淮，何豫我哉？」

translations.literal: Tao was timid and slow and could not use [the plan]; moreover, because he himself had not received an edict, he therefore said: "If they do no violence, let them cross the Huai—what concern is it of mine?"
translations.idiomatic: Tao was too timid to act and, having no orders from the throne, waved the danger away: "If they do no harm, let them cross the Huai—what is that to me?"

sentences.zh: 勛還，果盜徐州，其眾六七萬。

translations.literal: When Xun returned he indeed plundered Xuzhou; his host was sixty or seventy thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xun did turn on Xuzhou with a host of sixty or seventy thousand.

sentences.zh: 徐乏食，分兵攻滁、和、楚、壽，陷之，糧盡，啖人以飽。

translations.literal: Xuzhou lacked food; he divided troops to attack Chu, He, Chu, and Shou and took them; when grain was gone they ate men to be full.
translations.idiomatic: Starving Xuzhou, he sent columns against Chu, He, Chu, and Shou and seized them; when grain ran out his men ate human flesh to survive.

sentences.zh: 詔綯為徐州南面招討使。

translations.literal: An edict made Tao southern pacification commissioner facing Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The throne named Tao southern pacification commissioner against Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 賊方攻泗州，杜慆堅守，綯命湘率兵五千救之。

translations.literal: The bandits were then attacking Sizhou; Du Yin held firm; Tao ordered Xiang to lead five thousand troops to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were besieging Sizhou; Du Yin held the walls; Tao ordered Xiang to march five thousand men to its relief.

sentences.zh: 勛謾辭謝綯曰：「數蒙赦，所以未即降者，一二將為異耳，願圖去之，以身聽命。」

translations.literal: Xun sent a deceitful message of apology to Tao, saying: "I have repeatedly received pardon; the reason I have not at once surrendered is that one or two generals would be exceptions. I wish to plot removing them and will give my body to your command.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xun sent a smooth letter to Tao: "The throne has pardoned me again and again; I delay only because a few officers stand in the way. Remove them and I will submit in person.

sentences.zh: 綯喜，即請假勛節，而敕湘曰：「賊已降，第謹戍淮口，無庸戰。」

translations.literal: Tao was pleased and at once requested a false commission for Xun; and he instructed Xiang: "The bandits have surrendered—only guard the Huai crossing carefully; there is no need to fight."
translations.idiomatic: Tao rejoiced, sought a token commission for Pang Xun, and told Xiang: "The rebels have surrendered. Hold the Huai crossing and do not engage."

sentences.zh: 湘乃徹警釋械，日與勛眾歡言。

translations.literal: Xiang thereupon lifted the watch and laid aside weapons, daily sharing friendly talk with Xun's host.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang stood down the watches, stacked arms, and spent his days feasting with the rebel camp.

sentences.zh: 後賊乘間直襲湘壘，悉俘而食之，醢湘及監軍郗厚本。

translations.literal: Later the bandits seized an opening and struck straight at Xiang's camp; they captured all and ate them, and pickled Xiang and the army supervisor Chi Houben.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then rushed his camp, took every man alive, devoured them, and pickled Xiang and army supervisor Chi Houben.

sentences.zh: 時浙西杜審權使票將翟行約率千兵與湘會，未至而湘覆，賊偽建淮南旌幟誘之，亦皆陷。

translations.literal: At that time Zhexi's Du Shenquan had sent ticket-soldier commander Zhai Xingyue with a thousand troops to join Xiang; before they arrived Xiang was destroyed. The bandits raised Huainan banners as a ruse to lure them, and they too were all trapped.
translations.idiomatic: Du Shenquan of Zhexi had sent Zhai Xingyue with a thousand ticket troops to reinforce Xiang; before they arrived Xiang was gone. The rebels flew Huainan colors to lure them in and destroyed that force as well.

sentences.zh: 綯既師敗，乃以左衛大將軍馬舉代之。

translations.literal: After Tao's army was defeated he was replaced by Left Guard Grand General Ma Ju.
translations.idiomatic: After his defeat Tao was replaced by Left Guard Grand General Ma Ju.

sentences.zh: 以為太子太保，分司東都。

translations.literal: He was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with duty at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and kept at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 僖宗初，拜鳳翔節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xizong he was appointed military commissioner of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xizong's reign he was named military commissioner of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 頃之，就加同平章事，徙封趙。

translations.literal: Before long he was additionally made Associate Chief Minister and his fief was changed to Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was given the additional title Associate Chief Minister and his fief was shifted to Zhao.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十八，贈太尉。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-eight; posthumously he was made Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-eight and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 子滈、渙、沨。

translations.literal: Sons: Hao, Huan, and Feng.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Hao, Huan, and Feng.

sentences.zh: 綯子 滈滈避嫌不舉進士。

translations.literal: Tao's son Hao, to avoid suspicion, did not sit for the jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Tao's son Hao declined the jinshi examination lest he be thought to trade on family favor.

sentences.zh: 輔政，而滈與鄭顥為姻家，怙勢驕偃，通賓客，招權，以射取四方貨財，皆側目無敢言。

translations.literal: While [Tao] assisted in government, Hao was allied by marriage with Zheng Hao; relying on power he was arrogant and insolent, received guests freely, and gathered authority, shooting to seize goods and wealth from all quarters—everyone glared sideways and none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: While Tao held power, Hao married into Zheng Hao's clan and, trusting in his father's station, grew proud and grasping. He entertained clients, sold influence, and extorted wealth from every quarter until men watched in silence and none dared protest.

sentences.zh: 懿宗嗣位，數為人白髮其事，故去宰相。

translations.literal: When Yizong succeeded to the throne, many people repeatedly reported the affair, and therefore he left the post of chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yizong took the throne, the scandal was aired again and again until Linghu Chuo was forced from the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 因丐滈與群進士試有司，詔可，是歲及第。

translations.literal: Thereupon he begged that Hao might sit for the jinshi examination together with the assembled candidates before the authorities; the edict granted it, and that year he passed.
translations.idiomatic: Hao then petitioned to sit the jinshi with the rest of the candidates; the throne assented, and he placed that same year.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫崔瑄劾奏以十二月去位，而有司解牒盡十月，屈朝廷取士法為滈家事，請委御史按實其罪。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Adviser Cui Xuan memorialized impeachment: he left office in the twelfth month, yet the Board's release documents all bore the tenth month—bending the court's law for selecting scholars to serve Hao's household. He asked that censors be delegated to investigate and establish the crime.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Adviser Cui Xuan impeached him: Chuo had quit in the twelfth month, but the Board of Rites had backdated Hao's discharge papers to the tenth—warping the civil-service code for a family favor. Cui urged the censors to investigate and fix the offense.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: They did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The court took no action.

sentences.zh: 滈乃以長安尉為集賢校理。

translations.literal: Hao then, from Chang'an District Defender, became Collator of the Imperial Library at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was appointed from his post as defender of Chang'an district to collator in the Imperial Library.

sentences.zh: 稍遷右拾遺、史館修撰。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Right Reminder and Compiler in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In time he rose to Right Reminder and compiler in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 詔下，左拾遺劉蛻、起居郎張雲交疏指其惡，且言：「用李琢為安南都護，首亂南方，贓虐流著，使天下兵戈調斂不給。

translations.literal: When the edict went down, Left Reminder Liu Tuo and Attendant Gentleman Zhang Yun submitted successive memorials pointing to his wrongdoing, saying moreover: 'In appointing Li Zhuo Protectorate General of Annan, he first stirred chaos in the south; his greed and cruelty spread abroad, until the empire's armies and tax levies could not be supplied.
translations.idiomatic: After the appointment was announced, Left Reminder Liu Tuo and Attendant Gentleman Zhang Yun filed memorial on memorial denouncing him: 'By making Li Zhuo protector-general of Annan you loosed the first disorders in the south. His rapacity was notorious, and soon armies and revenue alike could not keep pace.

sentences.zh: 琢本進賂於滈，滈為人子，陷於惡，顧可為諫臣乎？」

translations.literal: Zhuo had originally advanced bribes to Hao; Hao, as a man's son, is sunk in evil—how can he yet serve as a remonstrance official?'
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo had bought his way in through bribes to Hao. A son who shares that stain—what claim has he to speak truth to power?'

sentences.zh: 又劾：「綯，大臣，當調護國本，而大中時，乃引諫議大夫豆盧籍、刑部侍郎李鄴為夔王等侍讀，亂長幼序，使先帝貽厥之謀幾不及陛下。

translations.literal: They further impeached: "Chuo is a great minister who ought to safeguard the foundation of the state, yet in the Dazhong era he brought in Remonstrance Adviser Dou Lu Ji and Vice Minister of Justice Li Ye as tutors to Prince Kui and the like, disordering the order of elder and younger and nearly keeping the late emperor's bequest from reaching Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: They went on: "As a chief minister Chuo should have guarded the succession. In the Dazhong years he installed Dou Lu Ji and Li Ye as tutors to Prince Kui, scrambling the line of precedence so that the late emperor's design almost never reached you.

sentences.zh: 且滈居當時，謂之『白衣宰相』。

translations.literal: Moreover, while Hao held sway in that age, people called him the 'White-Robbed Chancellor.'
translations.idiomatic: In those days men called Hao the 'chancellor in plain robes.'

sentences.zh: 滈未嘗舉進士，而妄言已解，使天下謂無解及第，不已罔乎？」

translations.literal: Hao had never sat for the jinshi, yet falsely said he had already been excused, making the realm believe one could pass without taking the examination—is this not deception?
translations.idiomatic: He had never truly sat the jinshi, yet boasted an exemption until the empire thought degrees could be won without the exam—is that not rank deceit?

sentences.zh: 滈亦懼，求換它官，改詹事府司直。

translations.literal: Hao also grew afraid and sought to exchange for another office, being changed to Court Gentleman of Directorship in the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: Hao, alarmed, asked for another post and was shifted to court gentleman in the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 方守淮南，上奏自治，帝為貶雲為興元少尹，蛻華陰令。

translations.literal: When Chuo was defending Huainan, he memorialized on his own conduct; the emperor for this demoted Zhang Yun to Vice Governor of Xingyuan and Liu Tuo to magistrate of Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: While Chuo held Huainan he sent up a memorial pledging self-restraint; the emperor punished the critics instead, demoting Zhang Yun to vice governor of Xingyuan and Liu Tuo to magistrate of Huayin.

sentences.zh: 滈亦湮厄不振死。

translations.literal: Hao also sank into hardship and died without rising again.
translations.idiomatic: Hao, too, languished in obscurity and died without recovering his standing.

sentences.zh: 綯子 渙、沨渙、沨皆舉進士，渙終中書舍人。

translations.literal: Chuo's sons Huan and Feng both entered the jinshi; Huan ended as Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo's sons Huan and Feng both took the jinshi; Huan finished his career as a drafter in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 弟 定定，字履常，楚弟。

translations.literal: Younger brother Ding, styled Lüchang, was a younger brother of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Ding, whose style was Lüchang, was a younger brother of Linghu Chu.

sentences.zh: 及進士第。

translations.literal: He also obtained the jinshi degree.
translations.idiomatic: He, too, passed the jinshi.

sentences.zh: 太和末，以駕部郎中為弘文館直學士。

translations.literal: In late Taihe, as Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites for chariotry he became a Bachelor of the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Taihe reign he served as vice director in the Ministry of Rites for chariotry and was made a bachelor of the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 李訓亂，王遐休方以是日就職，定往賀，為神策軍並收，欲殺者屢矣，已而免。

translations.literal: In Li Xun's turmoil, Wang Youxiu was just taking up his post on that very day; Ding went to congratulate him and was seized together by the Shence Army. Several times they were about to kill him, but in the end he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: During Li Xun's coup Wang Youxiu was taking office that same day; Ding went to offer congratulations and was swept up with him by the Shence Army. More than once they were ready to execute him, yet in the end he was released.

sentences.zh: 終桂管觀察使。

translations.literal: He ended as Observation Commissioner of Guiguan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office as military commissioner of Guiguan.

translations.literal: =Commentary=
translations.idiomatic: Commentary

sentences.zh: 贊曰：耽、佑、楚皆惇儒，大衣高冠，雍容廟堂，道古今，處成務，可也；

translations.literal: The Commentary says: Dan, You, and Chu were all earnest Confucians—great coats and high caps, composed in the ancestral hall, discoursing on past and present and handling established affairs; that much can be granted;
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Jia Dan, Du You, and Linghu Chu were grave Confucians in court robes, at ease in the ancestral hall, versed in antiquity and the business of state—so far, so fair;

sentences.zh: 以大節責之，蓋䃉中而玉表歟！

translations.literal: yet if one charges them with the great integrity, are they not perhaps rough stone within and jade without?
translations.idiomatic: but judged by the sternest standard of public virtue, were they not stone at the core beneath a jade polish?

sentences.zh: 悰、世當國，亦無足譏。

translations.literal: Cong and Shi, when they held the state, also had nothing much to be reproached for.
translations.idiomatic: When Linghu Cong and Linghu Shi governed, there was little worth reproach.

sentences.zh: 牧論天下兵曰：「上策莫如自治。」

translations.literal: Mu, in his discourse on military affairs throughout the realm, said: 'The highest policy is none like self-governance.'
translations.idiomatic: Du Mu, writing on the empire's armies, declared: 'The supreme strategy is to govern oneself well.

sentences.zh: 賢矣哉！

translations.literal: How worthy!
translations.idiomatic: How rightly spoken!
